title: Cloud Security Alliance CCSK
summary: The Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge, or CCSK, is the Cloud Security Alliance's foundational cloud security certification and the most widely recognised vendor neutral entry point into the field. It suits security analysts, architects, auditors and administrators who are moving into cloud work, and also developers and IT staff who need to understand how security changes when infrastructure is rented rather than owned. The open book, online multiple choice exam rewards understanding of the shared responsibility model, the Cloud Controls Matrix and the CSA security guidance rather than memorisation. It proves to an employer that you can reason about cloud risk across providers, and it pairs well with a hands on certification from one specific cloud vendor. It leads to roles such as cloud security analyst, cloud security engineer, security architect and cloud compliance specialist. The current curriculum, version five, lists twelve study areas; the chapters below group those areas into seven for readability while keeping their published names and order. Check the vendor's current version before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Cloud Security Alliance.

beginner.definition: This is an entry level cloud security certificate from the Cloud Security Alliance, a group that publishes free guidance about cloud computing. Its full name is Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge and the short name is CCSK. It is vendor neutral, which means it is not tied to Amazon, Microsoft or Google. It teaches how security work changes when a company rents computing instead of owning it.
beginner.whyItMatters: Almost every company now uses cloud services, but many security teams still think only about their own data centre. This certificate shows you understand the difference and can ask the right questions of a provider. It is often the fastest way to add cloud language to an existing security career. Because it is not tied to one vendor, it stays useful even if your employer changes platform. Many people take it before a deeper, provider specific certification.
howItWorks: Download the free Cloud Security Alliance guidance documents, because the exam is built directly around them.
Read the guidance once for understanding, then again while making your own summary notes for each study area.
Learn the shared responsibility model and the Cloud Controls Matrix, as they appear throughout the exam.
Study the key questions document from the European Union agency for cybersecurity, which covers legal and jurisdictional topics.
Take practice questions to check your recall, then revisit any study area where you score poorly.
The exam is taken online and is open book, but time pressure means you still need to know where to look quickly.
beginner.example: Think of the difference between cooking in your own kitchen and eating in a restaurant. At home you control the ingredients, the oven and the cleaning. In a restaurant you choose from a menu and trust the kitchen to handle food safely. You still decide what you order and who sits at your table. Cloud security is the same shift. You no longer control everything, so your job becomes asking the right questions, checking the answers and covering the parts the provider does not handle.
takeaways: The study material is free and public, so your main cost is time rather than textbooks.
Learn the shared responsibility model thoroughly, because nearly every other topic depends on it.
The exam is open book, so focus on understanding and on knowing where each answer lives in the guidance.

objectives: Describe cloud computing concepts, architectures and service models and their security effects
Apply the shared responsibility model to divide security duties between provider and customer
Assess governance, risk, audit and compliance obligations for services you do not fully control
Explain identity, access and data protection controls used in cloud environments
Evaluate cloud infrastructure, workload, application and monitoring security
Plan incident response, resilience and recovery for cloud dependent services

chapters.title: Cloud computing concepts and architectures
objectives: Explain the essential characteristics of cloud computing and what each one changes for security
Compare infrastructure, platform and software service models and the customer duties in each
Distinguish public, private, community and hybrid deployment models and their risk profiles
Describe the management plane and the data plane and why the management plane is a high value target
Apply the shared responsibility model to a given control, service or incident
Identify how virtualisation, containers and serverless computing change the attack surface

chapters.title: Cloud governance, risk, audit and compliance
objectives: Evaluate a provider's governance, risk and compliance posture before adoption
Adapt enterprise risk management processes to services you do not fully control
Manage legal, contractual and jurisdictional risk in multi provider environments
Map provider certifications and assurance reports such as SOC 2 to your compliance needs
Use the Cloud Controls Matrix to structure a control assessment
Plan an audit of a cloud service, gather credible evidence and track remediation

chapters.title: Organisation management and data governance
objectives: Define cloud roles, responsibilities and ownership across business and technology teams
Classify data so that protection matches its sensitivity and legal status
Define retention, deletion and discovery arrangements for data held by a provider
Assess where data physically resides and what that means for privacy obligations
Apply information lifecycle controls from creation through to secure disposal
Identify the risks created by copies of data spread across many cloud services

chapters.title: Identity and access management
objectives: Explain why identity is the primary security perimeter in cloud environments
Design federation, single sign on and role based access for users, services and devices
Apply least privilege and just in time access to administrative and management plane accounts
Protect secrets, keys and service credentials from exposure in code or configuration
Assess privileged access management controls and monitor for their misuse
Plan for compromise of an identity by limiting the blast radius of stolen credentials

chapters.title: Infrastructure, networking and workload security
objectives: Explain isolation, segmentation and network controls in a shared cloud platform
Assess encryption, key management and certificate handling for cloud workloads
Review hardening and vulnerability management for virtual machines and containers
Evaluate serverless and container orchestration security, including configuration risk
Judge the security of management interfaces and application programming interfaces
Apply immutable infrastructure and infrastructure as code practices safely

chapters.title: Data security, application security and security monitoring
objectives: Select encryption approaches such as provider managed, customer managed and client side keys
Build logging, monitoring and detection coverage for cloud hosted services
Integrate security checks into software development and deployment pipelines
Interpret alerts and findings from cloud native security tooling
Detect misconfiguration and inadequate change control, which are leading cloud risks
Use automation and policy as code to keep security controls consistent

chapters.title: Incident response, resilience and related technologies
objectives: Adapt incident response plans to a shared responsibility environment
Define evidence collection and forensic steps that work on cloud infrastructure
Test business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements for cloud dependencies
Plan for provider failure, service withdrawal and data portability
Assess the security impact of related technologies such as zero trust and the internet of things
Explain how emerging technology and regulation will change future cloud security work
